replication.target_description: Single replication experiment; omission-versus-commission immorality contrasts in both Tennis Tournament and Eyewitness scenarios, plus separate commission-before/after contrasts. Study label 1 and locator p.7 do not uniquely identify a contrast.

n.sample_role: Unresolved critical-test participant N; candidate study-wide N = 313, not adopted as analytic N.
n.exclusions: Supplementary p.3 explicitly states no data exclusions.
n.location: Main manuscript pp.8, 14, Tables 1–3 (pp.28–30); supplementary p.3. Supplied p.7 discusses extension constructs.
n.quote:
Participants were randomly

assigned to one condition in each of the two scenarios. ... The findings in The Tennis

Tournament scenario were in support of commission-omission asymmetry in immorality

attributions (pooled commission vs. omission: d = -0.45). ... The findings in The Eyewitness scenario regarding perceived immorality were very

similar for the main omission bias hypotheses contrasting commission and omission (d = -

0.47). ... Note. N = 313. ... There were no data exclusions. All data is included in the provided data.

notes: Only n_r is assigned; other fields and original side are unassigned placeholders. Identity: canonical text is a primary accepted author manuscript with full methods/results and supplementary materials. Cover title matches the neutral replication reference; authors John Jamison, Tijen Yay and Gilad Feldman match; cover states in press at Journal of Experimental Social Psychology, accepted March 09, 2020. Source URL identifies the same authors/year and replication manuscript. DOI 10.1016/j.jesp.2020.103977 is unprinted, so exact DOI identity is not independently confirmed. This is not an abstract-only parse or merely a preregistration. No PDF path supplied; no rendering/acquisition performed. Target ambiguity: supplied p.7 addresses causality, intentionality and regret rather than the immorality result. The single experiment includes two scenarios; study label 1 does not identify one scenario or contrast. Table 3 printed immorality candidates: Tennis Tournament pooled commission t = -3.65, p < .001, d = -0.45; commission-before t = -2.19, p = .030, d = -0.30; commission-after t = -4.34, p < .001, d = -0.60; Eyewitness commission t = -4.13, p < .001, d = -0.47. None selected as the assigned test. N evidence: p.8 reports 313 recruited participants, Table 1 reports N = 313 for correlations, and supplementary p.3 reports no exclusions. Keep this as candidate common-sample evidence only while correspondence is unresolved. Table 2 Tennis Tournament harm counts are after 51, before 51, pooled 101, omission 101; no-harm after 54, before 54, pooled 108, omission 54. These are inconsistent: 51 + 51 = 102 rather than pooled 101; do not correct the source or adopt a sum. Eyewitness mutually exclusive cells are 76, 79, 79, 79; candidate full-scenario sum 76 + 79 + 79 + 79 = 313 participants, no exclusions. Candidate only because the critical test is unresolved.
